title: Nepal celebrates Kukur Tihar as part of five-day Tihar festival - News On AIR
description: Nepal celebrates Kukur Tihar as part of five-day Tihar festival  News On AIR
publisher.title: News On AIR
full_article:
Nepal is celebrating its five-day festival of Tihar, which shares many traditions with Deepawali in India. Each day has its own significance, and today is dedicated to dogs on the occasion of Kukur Tihar.

Today, dogs are getting all the attention in Nepal. It is Kukur Tihar, a special day when people celebrate their love for these loyal companions. Marigold garlands are put around their necks, red tika is applied on their foreheads and special food is offered to them. From pet dogs to those living on the streets, dogs are welcomed into the celebrations and treated with affection.

According to Hindu beliefs, dogs are regarded as messengers of Yamaraj, the god of death. They are also associated with Lord Bhairav and are traditionally seen as guardians and protectors. This is why dogs hold a special place in the religious traditions behind Kukur Tihar.

The celebrations are also being observed at animal care centres. At Sneha’s Care, rescued and abandoned dogs are being given special food and affection. The centre provides shelter to animals in need and looks after them with care and attention.

This year, the celebrations are even more special as Kukur Tihar coincides with Laxmi Puja. While dogs are being honoured during the day, homes across Nepal will light up with oil lamps in the evening to welcome Goddess Laxmi. It brings together two important traditions of Tihar on the same day.

KATHMANDU, Nov 8: Nepal suffered their second consecutive defeat in the ACC Men's U-19 Asia Cup 2026, losing to the United Arab Emirates (UAE) by seven wickets in Oman on Sunday.

Having lost their opening match to India by 10 wickets, Nepal failed to bounce back as the UAE comfortably chased down the target of 154 runs in 34.4 overs, losing just three wickets.

The victory marked the UAE's first win in the tournament. Ayan Misbah led the UAE's chase with an unbeaten 75 runs. Kiran Rai contributed 32 runs, while Ahmed Khudadad and Omar Tauqir scored 24 and 11 runs, respectively.

For Nepal, captain Bipin Rawal, Nitesh Patel and Sushil Rawal took one wicket each.

Earlier, after losing the toss and being asked to bat at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Oman, Nepal were bowled out for 153 runs in 41 overs.

Sohail Kunwar was Nepal's top scorer with 33 runs, followed by Sachin Bhatt with 32. Niraj Kumar Yadav and Darsh Sonar contributed 16 runs each.

Naseem Khan was the standout bowler for the UAE, claiming five wickets for 43 runs in his eight overs, including one maiden.

Nepal will face Pakistan in their third match of the tournament on Tuesday.

title: Nepal clinches title of U-19 Women's Cricket Tournament - The Rising Nepal
description: Nepal clinches title of U-19 Women's Cricket Tournament  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
Kathmandu, Nov 8: The Nepal U-19 women's cricket team has won the Belt and Road Series held in China. Since today's final match against Hong Kong couldn't be completed due to rain, Nepal remained unbeaten and lifted the tournament trophy.

In the tournament with six teams participating, Nepal won four out of the six games they played. The remaining two games were canceled due to rain.

Nepal had a great start by beating Thailand by seven wickets in the first game of the series. Then, the second game against China ended without a result due to rain. In the third game, Nepal defeated Hong Kong by a big margin of 92 runs, and in the fourth game, they again beat Thailand by 52 runs.

In the fifth match, Nepal strengthened their title run by beating host China by 84 runs and then faced Hong Kong in the final game. Batting first in that match, Nepal had scored 88 runs for the loss of two wickets in 11 overs before the rain stopped the game.

After that, the game couldn't continue because of bad weather. Four teams participated in the tournament: Nepal, the hosts China, Hong Kong, and Thailand. (RSS)

title: Nepal’s peak electricity demand hits 1,813MW on Laxmi Puja evening - The Kathmandu Post
description: Nepal’s peak electricity demand hits 1,813MW on Laxmi Puja evening  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
Peak electricity demand on the national grid reached 1,813 megawatts on the evening of Laxmi Puja this year, exceeding the Nepal Electricity Authority’s forecast of around 1,700MW by 113MW.

According to data from the authority’s Load Dispatch Centre, total peak load on the system reached 2,400.30MW that evening. Peak electricity demand in the Kathmandu Valley stood at around 489.50MW, the centre said.

Despite the sharp rise in domestic demand, electricity supply remained smooth and uninterrupted, thanks to sufficient domestic generation.

Of the total 2,400.30MW available in the system, domestic consumption accounted for 1,813MW, while the surplus 587.30MW was exported to the Indian market, the authority said.

title: Diwali Celebrated Across Nepal with Lakshmi Puja and Deepavali - Ratopati
description: Diwali Celebrated Across Nepal with Lakshmi Puja and Deepavali  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. On the occasion of Tihar, the second largest festival of Nepalis, Diwali has been celebrated in homes across the country, including the capital, this evening to welcome Lakshmi.

The main day for Diwali on the occasion of Tihar is today. It is also called Deepamalika. Today, Diwali has been celebrated by cleaning windows, doors, rooms, thresholds, balconies, attics, and stairs.

It is believed that Lakshmi resides only in clean and well-painted houses. Based on this, the house was cleaned and painted with cow dung and red soil this morning, and Diwali was performed in the evening to invite Lakshmi.

The night of Kartik Krishna Aushi, when Lakshmi Puja is performed, is also called Sukharatri. This is one of the four major nights celebrated throughout the year. For Lakshmi Puja, the courtyard to the main door and the room where Lakshmi is established have been painted with cow dung and red soil, and Lakshmi's footprints have been made with rice flour and abir.

Dips have been lit in clay lamps or banana stalks at every step, making the villages and cities glitter. Currently, the practice of lighting candles has increased in place of 'lamps in clay pots'. According to religious scholar Prof. Toyaraj Nepal, lighting a lamp with oil is the Vedic tradition.

After performing Diwali, Lakshmi and Kuber are established in the puja room along with lamps, pots, and Ganesha, and Lakshmi is worshipped by offering jewelry, money, paddy, rice, fruits, selroti, and flower garlands.

After Lakshmi Puja, it is customary to worship young girls as a symbol of Lakshmi and give them dakshina. It is a religious belief that if Lakshmi is sent out of the house after performing Lakshmi Puja today, Lakshmi will leave.

Prof. Ramchandra Gautam informed that after the Lakshmi Puja, the women of the house perform a ritual of clapping sieves at midnight, wishing for 'Alakshmi to leave and for Lakshmi and prosperity to arrive'.

This evening, groups of young women have started playing Bhailo in various houses. It is a religious belief that Lord Vishnu was given the boon by King Bali to rule the three worlds – heaven, earth, and the underworld – for the five days of Yamapanchak.

title: Nepal Electricity Authority Manages Peak Demand During Laxmi Puja, Exports Power to India - Ratopati
description: Nepal Electricity Authority Manages Peak Demand During Laxmi Puja, Exports Power to India  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. Nepal Electricity Authority has stated that the peak demand for electricity on the occasion of Laxmi Puja this year has been successfully managed. While meeting the domestic electricity demand, electricity was exported to India today.

Nepal Electricity Authority stated that the peak demand of the national electricity system reached one thousand 813 megawatts at 6:15 PM on Sunday. The total peak load of the system at that time was two thousand 400 megawatts. Similarly, 587 megawatts of electricity was exported to India. There was zero megawatt interruption in the system.

Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation, Biraj Bhakta Shrestha, thanked the authority's employees, management, and general consumers for successfully managing the peak demand for electricity even when the system had suffered significant damage due to natural disasters.

Minister Shrestha had gone to the authority's load dispatch center on Sunday evening along with the Secretary of Energy, members of the authority's board of directors, and the authority's high management team to gather information about the demand and supply of electricity. Analyzing the electricity demand and supply data for the past three years on the occasion of Laxmi Puja, he stated that managing the demand in a challenging situation this year is a positive achievement.

He thanked the consumers for celebrating the festival of lights by using electricity safely and economically, and praised the contribution of the employees who worked day and night to ensure regular and reliable electricity supply. He urged the concerned bodies to work with equal commitment to make the electricity supply safe, reliable, and regular in the coming days.

According to the authority, during this year's Laxmi Puja, 1,536 megawatts of electricity was available to the system from independent power producers, 499 megawatts from the authority's subsidiary companies, 342 megawatts from the authority's run-of-river and semi-storage projects, and 22.30 megawatts from reservoir projects.

The authority stated that the demand was managed even with approximately 450 megawatts of electricity production from the Rasuwa region being out of the system due to natural disasters.

According to the authority's data, the peak demand for electricity during Laxmi Puja in 2082 BS reached one thousand 745 megawatts. Similarly, it was 1,602 megawatts in 2081 BS. This year's peak demand is 68 megawatts higher than last year. The electricity demand of the Kathmandu Valley has reached 489 megawatts. Last year it was 402 megawatts.

According to the authority's Executive Director, Dirghayu Kumar Shrestha, relevant bodies and technical teams across the country were kept on standby to ensure uninterrupted electricity supply. Necessary equipment including transformers and technical manpower were mobilized to immediately resolve any potential technical problems. He stated that teams were kept ready to resolve any issues within 15 minutes if they occurred in any location.

full_article:
The ninth artist in our Who Is series for the Eurovision Song Contest Asia 2026 is Pratik Himal Rai from Nepal.

Pratik Himal Mewahang Rai has over a decade of experience in the music industry. He also holds a bachelor’s degree in music.

In 2025, Rai competed in the sixth season of The Voice of Nepal . He made it through to the Knockouts before being eliminated. Shortly after his appearance on the show, he released his debut single “Chhaina maile”, a cover of the song by Karma Band that he performed in the Knockouts round of The Voice of Nepal .

This year, Rai released his second single “Jhari”. In September, he released his debut album “Poetry”.

Pratik Himal Rai was selected to represent Nepal at the Eurovision Song Contest Asia 2026 after winning Nepal Decides .

The song that Pratik will perform in Bangkok is called “Ananta Maya” (Infinite Love). It was written and composed by Pratik himself.

Pratik Himal Rai will perform in slot number 10 in the final of Eurovision Asia 2026.

The first edition of the Eurovision Song Contest Asia will take place at 19:30 ICT/14:30 CET on November 14 in Bangkok. Woody Milintachinda and Cindy Bishop will host the final. The winner will be determined by 50% jury voting and 50% public voting.

title: Vivek Ghosh: An Honour and a Privilege to Represent Nepal at LUNGO 2026 - Oncodaily
description: Vivek Ghosh: An Honour and a Privilege to Represent Nepal at LUNGO 2026  Oncodaily
publisher.title: Oncodaily
full_article:
Vivek Ghosh, Clinical Oncologist at Birat Cancer Institute, Nepal, Member of Two Worlds Cancer Collaboration, shared on LinkedIn:

“An honour and a privilege to represent Nepal at the Global Lung Cancer Congress (LUNGO 2026), sharing my insights on ‘ Redefining Lung Cancer Cure Through SBRT ‘ alongside leading global experts in lung cancer management including my teacher Dr. Avishek Shankar and wonderful senior Dr. Annie K Baa.

It was particularly fulfilling to speak on a subject close to my heart and passion, exploring how advances in Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy (SBRT) are reshaping the possibilities of curative-intent treatment in lung cancer.

Grateful to the organising committee for this wonderful opportunity and for bringing together a global community of experts dedicated to advancing lung cancer care.

Learning globally, sharing knowledge, and striving to make a difference locally.”
